chronic_neuropathic_pain.name: Chronic pain / neuropathic pain
chronic_neuropathic_pain.evidence_note: National Academies 2017: substantial evidence for chronic pain in adults. Newer reviews (Cochrane 2018, AHRQ/Annals 2026) find small improvements with real side-effect trade-offs.
chronic_neuropathic_pain.mechanism: THC acts on CB1 receptors in pain pathways of the spinal cord and brain, turning down pain signaling. The AHRQ review found comparable-ratio and high-THC products gave small pain gains while low-THC/high-CBD products may not help. Low-dose vaporized THC (1.29%) still beat placebo in neuropathic pain. Beta-caryophyllene is a terpene that binds CB2 (immune/inflammation) receptors and reduced neuropathic pain in mice without tolerance; that part is animal-only.
cautions: Benefits are modest; Cochrane notes harms may outweigh benefits for some people.
THC causes dizziness, sleepiness, impaired driving; start low.
Interactions with opioids, sedatives, and blood thinners; tell your doctor.

fibromyalgia.name: Fibromyalgia
fibromyalgia.evidence_note: Small trials only. Cochrane 2016 found no convincing high-quality evidence for nabilone; a 2023 systematic review calls the evidence low quality for short-term pain relief.
fibromyalgia.mechanism: In a controlled vapor study of four pharmaceutical varieties, only the balanced one (Bediol: 13.4 mg THC / 17.8 mg CBD) gave more patients a 30% pain drop than placebo (90% vs 55%). Pure THC (Bedrocan) and pure CBD (Bedrolite) did not beat placebo on main outcomes, and CBD seemed to blunt some of THC's analgesia. Nabilone (synthetic THC) improved sleep in a small fibromyalgia trial.
cautions: Single-dose and short trials; long-term benefit unknown.
Nabilone tolerability was low in fibromyalgia patients.
Watch for daytime drowsiness and mixing with other sedating meds.

ms_spasticity.name: Multiple sclerosis spasticity
ms_spasticity.evidence_note: Strong for patient-reported spasticity (National Academies: substantial; Cochrane 2022: nabiximols probably reduces spasticity short-term). Clinician-measured spasticity is weaker; a 2024 RCT missed its primary clinical endpoint.
ms_spasticity.mechanism: THC reduces muscle over-activity through CB1 receptors in the spinal cord; CBD in equal amounts is thought to soften THC's psychoactive side effects. In an enriched-design phase 3 trial, people who responded in the first 4 weeks kept the benefit vs placebo over 12 weeks; a 2023 meta-analysis supports add-on use for treatment-resistant spasticity.
cautions: Effects are modest (about 0.76 points on a 0-10 scale per National Academies).
Dizziness and falls risk; psychiatric and nervous-system side effects slightly more common.
Only about half of people respond in trials; stop if no benefit after a few weeks.

epilepsy.name: Epilepsy (Dravet, Lennox-Gastaut, TSC)
epilepsy.evidence_note: Strong, from multiple phase 3 RCTs of purified pharmaceutical CBD (Epidiolex) in Dravet, Lennox-Gastaut and tuberous sclerosis. Evidence for flower or artisanal oils is much weaker.
epilepsy.mechanism: CBD does not work mainly through CB1; it calms over-excited neurons through several targets (e.g., GPR55, TRPV1, adenosine signaling). In trials, adding CBD cut convulsive seizures in Dravet and drop seizures in Lennox-Gastaut more than placebo, and reduced TSC-associated seizures (25 mg/kg had better safety than 50).
cautions: Do not swap a prescribed anti-seizure drug for dispensary products; doses in trials were far higher and pharmaceutical-grade.
Liver enzyme elevations seen with CBD, especially with valproate; drug interactions (e.g., clobazam).
Store CBD oils vary widely in actual content.

insomnia.name: Insomnia
insomnia.evidence_note: A few small RCTs with mixed results. A THC+CBD oil helped; 150 mg CBD alone was about the same as placebo; CBN results are mixed.
insomnia.mechanism: THC shortens time to fall asleep via CB1 receptors. In a crossover RCT, an oil with 10 mg/ml THC + 15 mg/ml CBD improved sleep time and quality, and 60% no longer met insomnia criteria at 2 weeks. CBN: 20 mg nightly reduced awakenings in one RCT; a single 300 mg dose improved subjective sleep and sleep onset but not wake time after sleep onset. Myrcene had sedative effects in mice only.
cautions: Tolerance and rebound insomnia when stopping daily THC.
Next-day grogginess; do not drive.
CBD alone at 150 mg did not beat placebo on most sleep outcomes.

anxiety.name: Anxiety
anxiety.evidence_note: CBD shows promise in small trials (social anxiety public-speaking test; a 2024 meta-analysis). THC is biphasic and can cause anxiety. Lancet Psychiatry 2019 found scarce evidence overall.
anxiety.mechanism: CBD reduced anxiety from a simulated public-speaking test in people with social anxiety, toward healthy-control levels. In a 2024 human lab study, vaporized D-limonene added to THC selectively reduced THC-induced anxiety, so limonene-rich chemovars may make THC easier to tolerate. Linalool shows calming effects in mice only.
cautions: High THC can trigger or worsen anxiety and panic.
Heavy adolescent use is linked to later depression and suicidality.
CBD interacts with some antidepressants and benzodiazepines via liver enzymes.

ptsd.name: PTSD
ptsd.evidence_note: The first RCT of smoked cannabis in veterans found no active preparation beat placebo over 3 weeks. Nabilone for PTSD nightmares had a large effect in one small trial.
ptsd.mechanism: THC may weaken the replay of fear memories and suppress REM-sleep nightmares; CBD may help fear extinction. But in the veterans RCT (high-THC ~12%, high-CBD 11%, and ~8:8 THC+CBD) everyone improved including placebo. Nabilone showed the largest effect size for nightmares in a meta-analysis, from a single small study.
cautions: High THC can worsen anxiety, paranoia, and cannabis-use disorder risk, which is common in PTSD.
Not a replacement for trauma-focused therapy.
Psychosis risk with high-potency THC.

ibd_crohns.name: Crohn's disease / IBD
ibd_crohns.evidence_note: Small RCTs show symptom and quality-of-life improvement but no change in inflammation or endoscopic healing. Cochrane 2018: effects uncertain.
ibd_crohns.mechanism: Cannabinoids slow gut movement and ease cramping and pain, and CB2 activation can calm immune cells. In RCTs, THC-rich cannabis (8 weeks) and a 160/40 mg/ml CBD/THC oil both improved symptom scores, but neither healed the gut lining. Beta-caryophyllene reduced colitis in mice through CB2 and PPAR-gamma; animal-only.
cautions: Symptom relief can mask active inflammation; keep up with your GI doctor and scopes.
Not shown to induce remission.
Heavy long-term use is linked to cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome.

migraine.name: Migraine (acute attacks)
migraine.evidence_note: One recent crossover RCT is positive for vaporized THC+CBD flower; the rest is surveys.
migraine.mechanism: In the RCT, 6% THC + 11% CBD beat placebo for pain relief (67.2% vs 46.6%), pain freedom, and most-bothersome-symptom freedom at 2 hours, with benefit lasting to 24-48 hours. THC alone helped pain relief but not pain freedom. In a patient survey, a high-THC strain with dominant caryophyllene and myrcene (OG Shark) was most preferred; survey data only.
cautions: Frequent use of any acute headache treatment can drive more frequent headaches; discuss with your neurologist.
THC impairs driving.
Single trial; replication needed.

arthritis.name: Arthritis (rheumatoid and osteoarthritis)
arthritis.evidence_note: One small RA trial with nabiximols was positive; an oral CBD RCT in hand OA was negative; OA reviews rate evidence low quality.
arthritis.mechanism: Sativex (THC:CBD) gave a significant analgesic effect and lowered disease activity in the first controlled RA trial (small effect). Oral CBD in hand OA and psoriatic arthritis was no better than placebo. In rats, local CBD calmed early joint inflammation and prevented later OA pain and nerve damage.
cautions: Do not stop disease-modifying RA drugs.
Falls risk in older adults with THC.
Interactions with blood thinners and NSAIDs-adjacent meds; check with pharmacist.

cinv.name: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
cinv.evidence_note: National Academies: conclusive for oral cannabinoids. ASCO 2024 guideline: may help refractory nausea added to standard antiemetics. A 2024 phase II/III RCT confirmed THC:CBD benefit.
cinv.mechanism: THC acts on CB1 receptors in the brainstem vomiting center. Adding THC 2.5 mg + CBD 2.5 mg capsules to guideline antiemetics raised complete response from 8% to 24% in patients with refractory nausea.
cautions: Only as an add-on, coordinated with the oncology team.
More side effects (sedation, dizziness) than placebo.
ASCO advises against cannabis as a cancer treatment outside trials.

appetite_cachexia.name: Appetite loss / cachexia (cancer, HIV)
appetite_cachexia.evidence_note: National Academies: limited evidence for HIV/AIDS appetite and weight. Cancer cachexia meta-analysis: more appetite but worse quality of life from side effects.
appetite_cachexia.mechanism: THC triggers hunger signals through CB1 in the hypothalamus and improves food taste and smell; a cancer RCT found THC improved chemosensory perception and food enjoyment. Dronabinol improved appetite and reversed weight loss in HIV/AIDS. A THC-free CBG-rich extract made rats eat more; animal-only. THCV goes the other way and suppresses appetite.
cautions: Side effects can lower quality of life (cancer meta-analysis).
Sedation and confusion risk in frail or older patients.
Talk to the care team about interactions.
